notes: Volvo's media sites (media.volvocars.com, volvocars.com/…/media) returned 503/403; Volvo press releases were read from Volvo's Cision newsroom copies (news.cision.com).

Reveal: Volvo's release 'World premiere: the all-new Volvo XC90' is dated 27 August 2014 and German Wikipedia says the press presentation was in Stockholm on 27 August 2014; English Wikipedia says 26 August 2014. The interior had been shown first, on 27 May 2014.
Power figures in the 2014 Volvo release are 'hp' (metric); English Wikipedia gives the D5 as 235 hp. Volvo's figures are recorded.

The T8 was renamed 'Recharge' for the 2021 model year and received a more powerful 107 kW electric motor and an 18.8 kWh battery in 2021 (Wikipedia). In March 2024 the XC90 was the last Volvo built with a diesel engine (Wikipedia). Not recorded as separate revisions.

EX90: Wikipedia says the electric EX90 was introduced in late 2022 as the XC90's successor, but in September 2024 Volvo said both would be sold together. The EX90 is a separate model and is not included here.

No manufacturer dimensions, cargo volumes or model-year-specific outputs (B5/B6, T8 Recharge 455 hp) were readable; dimensions are from English Wikipedia (model year not stated). The 2026 long-range PHEV update's system output was not stated in the release.

Seating: Volvo describes the second generation as a '7-seater'; Wikipedia and Volvo's 2019 release also describe 5-seat (dropped after the 2017 model year), 4-seat Excellence (2017–2020) and 6-seat (from the 2020 model year) layouts in words only, so only 7 is recorded in the seating field.

Volvo Germany's 2023 and 2024 releases give 4,953 mm length, 1,771 mm height and 2,984 mm wheelbase (width 2,140 mm incl. mirrors) and a maximum 1,816 L load volume; these use German thousands separators ('4.953', '1.816') which the quote checker cannot match as numbers, so they are not recorded as fields. The Wikipedia figures (4,950 mm length, 1,776 mm height) differ slightly.
